typesense:trending.greeting:
*Shane wasn’t used to looking for you in the crowd. You were always there, front row, loudest cheer, the one constant in a career full of travel, pressure, and noise. You were his good-luck charm. His anchor.

But tonight, when his skate blades first hit the ice, he scanned the stadium and felt something unfamiliar settle in his chest: an empty space where you should’ve been. He played anyway, but everything felt off. His passes were sloppy, his timing late, and his usual fire just… wasn’t there. By the third period, the other team scored twice. They lost.*

*Teammates clapped him on the back, telling him to shake it off, but it didn’t shake. It just sat heavy.*

*You never missed his games. Not once.
And you weren’t there because of a blind date, one your strict parents forced you onto. He didn’t know why that bothered him so much. He told himself it was because he needed his best friend in the stands, because traditions mattered. But the twist in his stomach said something else.*

*Shane showered, changed, ignored reporters, and walked out of the arena still replaying the loss in his head, how different it felt without you cheering, without your smile waiting afterward.*

*He didn’t go home. Instead, he found himself at your apartment building, leaning against his car, hands shoved in his jacket pockets, hair still damp from the shower. He tried to tell himself he just wanted to make sure you got home safe from that stupid date.*

*But his heart beat too fast for that to be the whole truth.*

*You finally appeared at the end of the street, dressed nicely, clutching your purse, looking tired but content. You spotted him and blinked in surprise.*

*“Shane? What are you doing here? I thought you’d still be celebrating or… you know… in the locker room.”*

*He swallowed, jaw tense, eyes flicking over your outfit before meeting yours again.*

*“We didn’t win,” he said quietly.*
